rounds.fact: IMDb started in 1990 as a hobbyist mailing list of movie trivia before becoming a website, and is still one of the oldest continuously running sites on the entire internet.
Zillow launched in 2006 and was one of the first sites to give the public free access to home value estimates, a feature ('Zestimate') that unsettled a lot of real estate agents at the time.
Yelp started in 2004 as an email-based referral service before pivoting to the review-website format it's known for today, after users kept asking for a public place to post reviews.
Webshots was one of the most popular photo-sharing communities of the early 2000s, and was also widely used as a source for desktop wallpaper downloads.
Break.com built its early audience around viral videos aimed specifically at young men, a more niche focus than general-purpose video sites like YouTube.
